# Submit Memory Feedback with the Mem0 Platform Python SDK

## Background

Mem0 is a managed memory layer for LLM agents. After storing memories with `MemoryClient.add(...)`, products can submit feedback on individual memories using `MemoryClient.feedback(memory_id, feedback, feedback_reason)` so that the underlying ranker can improve. The feedback enum supports `POSITIVE`, `NEGATIVE`, and `VERY_NEGATIVE`.

In this task you must write a small Python program that ingests a short conversation into Mem0, retrieves the extracted memories for a unique scoped user, submits one feedback record per memory (cycling through the three feedback types), and writes a structured log so the run can be audited.

## Requirements

* Use the Mem0 Platform Python SDK (`from mem0 import MemoryClient`) — the script must hit the real managed API using the `MEM0_API_KEY` environment variable. Do not mock the SDK.
* Read the run identifier from the `ZEALT_RUN_ID` environment variable and use it to derive a unique `user_id` so concurrent runs do not collide.
* Add a short, deterministic conversation (provided below) to Mem0 under that scoped `user_id`.
* After the add call, list the resulting memories for the user using `client.get_all(...)` so you can capture the server-assigned memory IDs.
* For each stored memory, submit one feedback record using `client.feedback(...)`. Cycle through the feedback types in this order — first memory: `POSITIVE`, second: `NEGATIVE`, third: `VERY_NEGATIVE` — and provide a non-empty `feedback_reason`. If Mem0 produces fewer than three memories from the conversation, cycle through the feedback types in the same order across whichever memories do exist.
* Write a structured log file recording every feedback submission so it can be verified.

## Implementation Hints

* Build the scoped user with the pattern `feedback-user-${ZEALT_RUN_ID}`.
* Memory extraction in the managed API is asynchronous; after `client.add(...)` returns you may need to wait briefly (poll `client.get_all(...)` until it returns memories, or sleep) before the IDs are available.
* The Python SDK exposes a `feedback(memory_id=..., feedback=..., feedback_reason=...)` method that returns a JSON-serialisable dict containing the feedback `id`.
* Use `client.get_all(filters={"user_id": "feedback-user-${ZEALT_RUN_ID}"}, version="v2")` so the response is the v2 envelope with stable IDs.
* Keep the script idempotent enough to retry on transient failures; verification will only inspect the final log file and the live state in Mem0.

## Conversation to ingest

```
role=user    content="My name is Robin and I'm planning a trip to Kyoto next April."
role=assistant content="Lovely! I'll keep that in mind for your itinerary."
role=user    content="I'm vegetarian, so please remember to flag vegetarian restaurants."
role=assistant content="Got it, I'll only recommend vegetarian-friendly places."
role=user    content="Also, I tend to wake up early and prefer morning activities."
```

## Acceptance Criteria

* Project path: /home/user/myproject
* Ensure the real Mem0 actions (add memories and submit feedback) are executed against the managed Mem0 Platform; do not mock the API.
* The scoped user identifier passed to Mem0 must be exactly `feedback-user-${ZEALT_RUN_ID}` where `ZEALT_RUN_ID` is read at runtime from the environment.
* Log file: /home/user/myproject/feedback.log
* The log file must exist after the run and contain exactly one line per feedback submission, with this format (one record per line, in the same order feedback was submitted):

  ```
  memory_id=<uuid> feedback=<POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|VERY_NEGATIVE> feedback_id=<uuid>
  ```

  * `<uuid>` values must be the actual UUID strings returned by Mem0 (lower-case, hyphenated).
  * At least three records must be present and the feedback types must appear in the order `POSITIVE`, `NEGATIVE`, `VERY_NEGATIVE` for the first three records. If more than three memories are produced, additional records may continue cycling through the same three values.
  * All `memory_id` values in the log must correspond to memories that exist in Mem0 under the scoped `user_id`.
* The Mem0 project, when queried via `client.get_all(filters={"user_id": "feedback-user-${ZEALT_RUN_ID}"}, version="v2")`, must return at least one memory.
